label: DMZ Perimeter Gateway
info: The DMZ perimeter gateway filters inbound traffic, hosts load balancers and reverse proxies, and isolates external connections from the corporate network. Attackers target exposed web applications and SSL-VPN vulnerabilities here to gain initial access.

label: Active Directory Domain Controller Hub
info: The Tier-0 identity core managing Kerberos authentication, LDAP policies, and domain trusts. Target for Kerberoasting, AS-REP Roasting, and Golden Ticket generation upon credential compromise.

label: Secure Administrative Workstations
info: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) with hardware MFA. If administrators log into lower-tier systems from these machines, their cached Kerberos credentials in LSASS can be harvested by attackers.

label: Application Servers Cluster
info: Tier-1 microservices and internal web applications. Often run under custom service accounts with registered Service Principal Names (SPNs), making them prime targets for Kerberoasting ticket cracking.

label: Database Storage Cluster
info: High-value business data repository (MSSQL/MySQL). Accessed through database links or service delegation. Unconstrained delegation on application servers can expose this tier to unauthorized impersonation.

label: SIEM & Security Telemetry (SOC)
info: Aggregates audit events (Sysmon, Event ID 4624/4625, NetFlow). Blue teams rely on these telemetry pipelines for detecting lateral movement, pass-the-hash techniques, and anomalous LDAP queries.

label: Secure VPN Gateway
info: Remote access ingress point. Weak password policies, absence of multi-factor authentication, or session hijacking can allow external adversaries to tunnel directly into internal subnets.
